purpose: Per-group receive-engine state machine implementing fsm.md's authoritative transition table (L1-L11, H1-H2, the {lifecycle,health} pair, the gap-free catching_up->buffering_live->live cutover protocol, the T_join=8000ms joining-gate with background-continue/late-merge, and the L8/L9 epoch-triggered deferred-retry flow). Companion module ingest-policy.ts wraps a PendingRetryQueue-equivalent (dedupe + bounded-retry-budget deferred queue), consumed exclusively by receive-engine.ts. The engine drives ingest via the IngestSource control interface (catchUp/openLive/ingestPersisted/close), consumes marmot-free IngestSignals, and persists through the PersistenceAdapter seam -- S4's real fact/accepted-event methods plus S11-owned checkpoint/deferred methods (mocked here, MOCK-05-002).

public_api.name: createReceiveEngine
public_api.description: Factory. Constructs a per-group engine instance in lifecycle 'uninitialized', health 'nominal'. No I/O happens until start() is called.

public_api.name: ReceiveEngine.start
public_api.description: Only callable from lifecycle 'uninitialized' (throws otherwise). origin:'welcome' always routes to L2 joining. origin:'restored' evaluates the reconciled L1/L2 guard (see judgment call 'l1-l2-restart-routing'). The returned promise resolves once the deterministic portion of the initial transition chain settles (it does NOT await an in-flight T_join background bootstrap continuation past a timeout -- callers must not block UI rendering on this promise; use subscribe() for progress).

public_api.name: ReceiveEngine.stop
public_api.description: L10. Idempotent (no-op if already 'stopped' or 'uninitialized'). Unsubscribes the live subscription, calls adapter.close() as its final adapter interaction, sets lifecycle='stopped'/health='nominal', persists a final checkpoint.

public_api.name: ReceiveEngine.reset
public_api.description: L11. Callable from any lifecycle. Defensively unsubscribes any open live subscription (in-memory hygiene; does NOT call adapter.close() -- that remains stop()'s exclusive responsibility per fsm.md's L10/L11 action split), clears all in-memory bookkeeping (lastEpoch, lastIngestedSeq, lastAcceptedDomainEventId, bootstrapCompleted, degradation reasons, ingest-policy dedupe+deferred state), calls persistence.clearGroupState(groupId), and lands in 'uninitialized'/'nominal' WITHOUT a trailing saveCheckpoint call (a post-clear checkpoint write would leave a non-null checkpoint behind, contradicting clearGroupState's 'loadCheckpoint returns null after' postcondition).

public_api.name: ReceiveEngine.subscribe
public_api.description: Registers a listener for all ten EngineOutputEvent variants. Returns an unsubscribe function.

public_api.name: createRealEngineScheduler
public_api.description: Production EngineScheduler backed by the global setTimeout/clearTimeout/Date.now. The sole sanctioned call site for these globals in src/engine/ (mirrors src/domain/task-events.ts's precedent of confining nondeterministic calls to one documented factory).

public_api.name: EngineScheduler (interface)
public_api.signature: { now(): number; setTimeout(fn: () => void, ms: number): EngineTimerHandle; clearTimeout(handle: EngineTimerHandle): void }
public_api.description: Injected timer/clock abstraction (constructor dep) so T_join and periodic-checkpoint timing are test-controllable via a fake implementation (vitest fake timers, wrapped) without the engine ever referencing Date/setTimeout globals directly.

public_api.name: StartOptions / EngineOrigin
public_api.signature: type EngineOrigin = 'restored' | 'welcome'; interface StartOptions { origin: EngineOrigin }
public_api.description: Not re-exported from engine-types.ts (frozen, S1-owned, out of this story's scope.includes) -- owned here as receive-engine.ts's own public-surface addition, matching the module map's 'new construction; explicit start()/stop()/reset() lifecycle' ownership grant.

public_api.name: ReceiveEngineDeps
public_api.signature: interface ReceiveEngineDeps { groupId: string; adapter: IngestSource; persistence: PersistenceAdapter; scheduler: EngineScheduler; tJoinMs?: number; checkpointIntervalMs?: number; ingestPolicyOptions?: IngestPolicyOptions }
public_api.description: Constructor deps. tJoinMs defaults to 8000 (fsm.md T_join). checkpointIntervalMs defaults to 30000 (periodic live-phase save, AC-FSM-4). ingestPolicyOptions defaults to ingest-policy.ts's DEFAULT_INGEST_POLICY_OPTIONS.

owned_data: In-memory: lifecycle, health-degradation-reason set, lastEpoch, lastIngestedSeq, lastAcceptedDomainEventId, bootstrapCompleted flag, pendingBootstrapReinfer flag, live-signal buffer, live-subscription unsubscribe handle, checkpoint periodic-save timer handle, an ingest-policy instance (dedupe-processed-id set + deferred/retry-budget queue) -- exactly the module map's 'Lifecycle state, lastEpoch, retry budget, PendingRetryQueue (in-memory)' grant.
dependencies_allowed: src/engine/engine-types.ts (EngineState/EngineLifecycleState/EngineHealth, EngineCheckpoint, EngineOutputEvent, IngestSignal, IngestSource, PersistenceAdapter, RawProtocolFact/RawProtocolFactInput/AppendFactResult, AcceptedDomainEvent, DeferredReason, Unsubscribe -- all type-only plus the frozen interfaces this story consumes, never modifies)

src/domain/domain-events.ts (deriveMlsAcceptedEventId, deriveBootstrapAcceptedEventId, SOURCE_KIND_PHASE_ORDER -- per the story's explicit 'import DIRECTLY, engine-types re-exports types only' instruction)
src/domain/task-events.ts (TaskEvent type only, for the local taskIdOf(payload) helper that distinguishes task.created's payload.task.id from every other variant's payload.taskId)
dependencies_forbidden: src/marmot/* (including src/marmot/ingest-queue.ts -- see judgment call 'ingest-policy-cannot-import-marmot-ingest-queue' for why the story text's 'wrap the existing PendingRetryQueue' is honored in algorithm, not in import)
src/persistence/* (the engine calls PersistenceAdapter methods on an injected instance; it never imports an implementation file)
src/domain/task-projector.ts and src/domain/task-crdt.ts (the engine stays projection-free by design -- see judgment call 'engine-stays-projection-free')
external_ports: IngestSource (consumed: catchUp, openLive, ingestPersisted, close) -- MOCK-05-001 in this story's tests, real S7 marmot-adapter.ts later, zero receive-engine.ts changes required at that swap per the interface boundary

PersistenceAdapter (consumed: all ten methods -- appendFact/loadFacts/appendAcceptedEvent/loadAcceptedEvents are REAL S4 raw-event-log-store.ts semantics in integration-style tests; saveCheckpoint/loadCheckpoint/saveDeferredIds/loadDeferredIds/acceptDeferredFact/clearGroupState are MOCK-05-002 here, real S11 checkpoint-store.ts/deferred-store.ts later)

judgment_calls.decision: The story brief says ingest-policy.ts wraps 'the existing PendingRetryQueue (from src/marmot/ingest-queue.ts -- READ it; wrap, don't rewrite)'. architecture.md's Boundary Rules (Forbidden Rule 5, added S2 Stage-2 cold review P2-8) and engine-boundary.structural.test.ts's AC-BOUND-1 scanner explicitly and unconditionally forbid ANY src/engine/* file from importing anything matching '/marmot/' -- verified by reading the scanner source directly (disallowedCategory() flags any specifier containing '/marmot/', with a scanner-liveness fixture proving it flips to failing on exactly this import shape) and by the story's own gate text ('the engine boundary structural suite auto-covers your new files -- they must pass it as-is'). A literal import is therefore not an option; the structural, review-blocking gate outranks the story prose. Resolved by PORTING createPendingRetryQueue's algorithm (dedupe-by-id Map preserving insertion order, cap-with-evict-eldest, TTL-prune) into a new, engine-native implementation in ingest-policy.ts operating on RawProtocolFact + factId (never importing applesauce-core's NostrEvent or crossing into src/marmot/). This mirrors engine-types.ts's own S1 precedent of declaring a structural NostrEvent type rather than importing applesauce-core's for the identical boundary reason (see engine-types.ts's NostrEvent doc comment). 'Wrap, don't rewrite' is honored in the sense that matters for review -- proven algorithm shape, not a duplicated-and-diverged reimplementation -- while remaining structurally compliant.

Per the story's explicit framing ('Constraint 7 puts incremental projection in the integration layer; the engine may stay projection-free -- decide and document'), receive-engine.ts holds NO in-memory TaskProjection and never imports task-projector.ts/task-crdt.ts. It emits domain_event_accepted (and the other nine EngineOutputEvent variants); folding into a TaskProjection is the integration layer's job (S8 react-engine-hooks.ts, per Implementation Constraint 7's applyEvent(currentProjection, event.payload) mandate). This story's tests independently fold emitted events with the real task-projector.applyEvent to stand in for that consumer when an AC's observable talks about 'the projection' (AC-FSM-3, AC-INV-5) -- the fold happens in test code, never inside the engine.

IngestSource (frozen by S1, out of this story's scope to modify) exposes exactly four methods -- catchUp, openLive, ingestPersisted, close -- with no dedicated bootstrap-fetch method, yet fsm.md's L2 entry action says 'begin bootstrap snapshot fetch with timeout T_join' and L4/L5's guards are bootstrapResolved/bootstrapTimedOut/bootstrapFailed. Resolved by treating the joining-phase bootstrap fetch as ONE adapter.catchUp() call, raced against an 8000ms scheduler.setTimeout: bootstrapResolved = the async iterable completes before the timer; bootstrapTimedOut = the timer fires first (the iterable is NOT cancelled -- it keeps draining signals through the SAME shared per-signal handler in the background; when it eventually completes, its late resolution clears the 'bootstrap-unresolved' degradation reason, restoring health:nominal per H2, exactly as fsm.md's Joining-timeout section describes for the un-cancelled fetch); bootstrapFailed = the iterable rejects before the timer. On EVERY entry into catching_up (L3 from recovering, L4/L5 from joining) the engine performs its OWN fresh openLive()+catchUp() cycle (the cutover-protocol drain, AC-FSM-2) -- this is a SEPARATE, second catchUp() call from the joining-phase bootstrap fetch, not a reuse of the same iterable. Documented rather than silently decided because it is the one place this story's design fills a gap the frozen IngestSource contract left open.

Implements the reconciled fsm.md L1/L2 guard verbatim as specified in this story's brief: L1 (recovering) iff (a usable, shape-valid checkpoint with bootstrapCompleted===true) OR (an absent/corrupt checkpoint with a non-empty raw-log or accepted-log -- preserve-and-replay, lastIngestedSeq forced to 0, health degraded via a 'preserve-and-replay-recovery' reason that clears specifically at the FIRST checkpoint save coincident with reaching live, which also re-infers bootstrapCompleted=true at that same moment). L2 (joining) otherwise: origin='welcome' unconditionally, OR origin='restored' with a usable checkpoint whose bootstrapCompleted===false, OR an absent/corrupt checkpoint with BOTH logs empty. loadCheckpoint's return is additionally shape-validated (isValidCheckpoint) so a deserialize-succeeded-but-malformed value is treated identically to null/thrown, matching Implementation Constraint 12.

S5's acceptance criteria are AC-FSM-1..8 and AC-INV-5 only; AC-REC-1..9 (Recovery Sequencing) belong to a later story (S11, which also resolves MOCK-05-002's checkpoint/deferred mocking). This story's 'recovering' entry action still performs a functionally coherent R1-R3 pass (loads rawLog/acceptedLog/deferredIds via the mocked persistence methods, prunes+rebuilds the ingest-policy deferred queue per R2a/R2, marks every already-accepted id as processed so R3's full-log resubmission on a corrupt-checkpoint path cannot re-emit a duplicate domain_event_accepted, and resubmits only rawLog facts with seq>lastIngestedSeq via adapter.ingestPersisted per R3) so that L1 is a real, FSM-conformant transition rather than a decorative label -- but it is not held to AC-REC's exact observables (e.g. it does not independently prove R-INV-4's crash-plus-continuation equality). Flagged as an explicit S11 follow-up obligation, not a silent gap.

engine.start() awaits the full deterministic transition chain UP TO the point where the FSM is genuinely waiting on an outstanding external operation it cannot control the timing of. Concretely: the T_join timeout branch runs as a detached async continuation (fired from the injected scheduler's setTimeout callback, not part of start()'s own await chain), so start()'s returned promise does not resolve at the 8000ms degraded-transition point -- it resolves only once the underlying bootstrap catchUp() iterable itself eventually settles (success, late-merge, or failure), which may be arbitrarily later. This matches real usage: a caller (S8's react-engine-hooks.ts) must not block UI rendering on awaiting start() to observe a slow/hung relay; it should call start() and observe progress via subscribe(). Tests in this story that need to observe the mid-flight degraded transition therefore do NOT await start() directly -- they let it run detached (start().catch(()=>{})) and drive fake timers, matching this documented contract rather than fighting it.

amendments.note: JUDGMENT-CALL SUPERSEDED (Stage-1 review sev-6 resolution): the "IngestSource exposes exactly four methods / bootstrap = catchUp raced against T_join" judgment call reflects the ORIGINAL implementation, which review rejected as unsound (concurrent stateful catchUp drains). The landed design: IngestSource has FIVE methods — fetchBootstrap(): AsyncIterable<IngestSignal> is the dedicated joining-phase bootstrap channel (NIP-44, ratchet-free, overlap-safe, no-abandonment-on-timeout); catchUp() runs exactly once per start(), runtime-guarded. See engine-types.ts IngestSource JSDoc (the S7-binding contract) and architecture.md IngestSource table.
